root_cause.trajectory_summary: The agent identified that the exploit relies on overriding a Guice-provided @JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig during JSON deserialization (via an empty-string key) and implemented a mitigation by forcing Jackson to ignore any input value for the injected parameter. In turns 31–33 it verified the code changes and generated a patch file from the git diff into /root/patches. In turn 34 the required Maven build failed due to an unavailable apache-jar-resource-bundle:1.5-SNAPSHOT referenced by the maven-remote-resources-plugin. The agent investigated the pom.xml (turns 35–36), confirmed Maven Central has released versions (turn 38), patched pom.xml to use 1.5 (turn 40), wrote a second patch file for that build fix (turn 42), and then rebuilt successfully with the specified Maven command (turn 43). Final state: two patch files exist under /root/patches/, the /root/druid working tree contains the applied fixes, and the relevant JARs were built successfully (turn 44).

what_worked.item: Created the vulnerability fix by updating all JavaScriptConfig injection sites to disable input override: e.g., turn 31 shows “- @JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig config” changed to “+ @JacksonInject(useInput = OptBoolean.FALSE) JavaScriptConfig config”, with OptBoolean imported.

Wrote the vulnerability patch file to the required directory: turn 32 shows “git --no-pager diff > /root/patches/0001-druid-0.20.0-disable-jacksoninject-useinput-for-js.patch” and the file listed in /root/patches.

Diagnosed the Maven build failure cause accurately: turn 34 error “Could not find artifact ... apache-jar-resource-bundle:jar:1.5-SNAPSHOT” and turns 35–36 locate the exact pom.xml resourceBundle entry.
Validated that a non-snapshot release exists on Maven Central: turn 38 fetches maven-metadata.xml showing versions including 1.5, 1.7, 1.8.
Applied an environment build fix and captured it as a separate patch: turn 40 replaces “1.5-SNAPSHOT” with “1.5”, and turn 42 writes /root/patches/0002-druid-0.20.0-build-fix-resource-bundle.patch.

Successfully rebuilt Druid with the requested Maven command after the pom fix: turn 43 ends with “BUILD SUCCESS” for the reactor modules including druid-processing, druid-server, and druid-indexing-service.
Confirmed the expected built artifacts exist: turn 44 lists the built JARs under /root/druid/*/target/ including processing/core/server/indexing-service.

issue.evidence: The Maven build failed: “Resources archive cannot be found.: Could not find artifact org.apache.apache.resources:apache-jar-resource-bundle:jar:1.5-SNAPSHOT ...” and the reactor stopped at the root pom module.
issue.cause: The upstream pom.xml references a SNAPSHOT artifact (1.5-SNAPSHOT) for the maven-remote-resources-plugin resource bundle, which was not available from the configured repositories in this environment.

issue.evidence: The tool rejected a command containing multiple separate commands: “Cannot execute multiple commands at once.”
issue.cause: Incorrect tool usage (multiple commands not chained with && or ;), requiring the agent to rerun the steps as separate tool calls.

issue.evidence: The agent did not demonstrate (in the trace) an actual HTTP exploit attempt pre/post patch or a unit/integration test proving that sampler requests with an empty-string key are rejected while legitimate requests pass.
issue.cause: The run focused on static hardening (Jackson annotation change) and successful compilation; functional validation was left to the external verifier, so correctness is inferred rather than directly observed in the trace.

root_cause.outcome_assessment: The required patch files were created under /root/patches/, the corresponding code and pom changes are present in /root/druid, and the specified Maven build completed successfully (turn 43), though exploit-blocking behavior was not directly exercised in the trace.
